verdict.rationale: The pack never names an official SDK or client library. The closest evidence is workflows-as-code, where orchestration logic is written directly in TypeScript or Python with Windmill handling checkpointing and parallelism, which implies a first-party language library. Full-code React/Svelte frontends connected to Windmill backend runnables also suggest a programmatic interface. The CLI and MCP server are separate interfaces, and the OpenAPI spec probe returned 404 on every candidate path. Missing for 10: explicitly documented official SDKs (named packages per language), SDK reference docs, a published API spec for generated clients, and independent or hands-on corroboration of SDK use.
